full_judgment:
"I. Because, it is an error apparent on the face of the Judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division that the Hon'ble Court failed to appreciate that the learned Arbitrator filed the Award in time as per direction dated 12.06.2005 of the Hon'ble Appellate Division passed in C.P.L.A No. 387 of 2005 and accordingly following the Order dated 03.08.2005 of the trial Court, so, the findings of the trial Court in acceptance of 'Written Objection' condoning the limitation on the point of sufferings of Award illegalities are not sustainable at all. The Hon'ble Appellate Division also failed to take into consideration that the Arbitration proceeding was stayed for more than one and half years at the instance of the defendant by the apex Court. 

 III. Because, it is an error apparent on the face of the Judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division that the Hon'ble Court failed to appreciate that as the learned trial Court duly notified both the parties regarding submission of Award before the Court which were duly acknowledged by the learned lawyers of both the parties on 29.08.2005 by putting their signatures and by writing "Seen" in the left margin of Order Sheet dated 27.08.2005 and subsequently the defendant prayed for time for filing Written Objection ignoring the point of limitation, in that case notice as contemplated by Section 14(2) of the Arbitration Act is liable to be dispensed. The Hon'ble Appellate Division also failed to take into consideration that mode of notice is not mentioned in the law. So, definite knowledge subject to authentication can be the best form of notice. As such, the impugned Judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division ought to be interfered by this Hon'ble Court. 

 IV. Because, it is an error apparent on the face of the Judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division that the Hon'ble Court failed to appreciate that the defendant on 29.08.2005 came to know about submission of Award by putting their signatures and by writing "Seen" in the left margin of Order Sheet dated 27.08.2005 and subsequently the defendant on 03.09.2005, 06.09.2005 and 21.09.2005 prayed for time for filing their 'Written Objection' ignoring the point of limitation. Lastly, on 09 10.2005 and 14.11.2005 (i.e. 41 days and 77 days later of their knowledge of submission of Award) they filed their Written Objections' before the trial Court against the Award without depositing any security, which is beyond the period of 30 days limitation as per Article 158 of the Limitation Act. The Appellate Division also failed to take into consideration that the Arbitration Act is a special law, as such there is no scope to condone the delay. 'Written Objection' ought to be filed wit;-till 30 days from the date of knowledge of submission of Award before the Court as per Article 158 of the Limitation Act. So, the Plaintiffs application dated 23.01.2006 with a prayer for rejection of defendant's 'Written Objections' ought to be allowed for ends of justice. As such, the impugned Judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division ought to be interfered by this Hon'ble Court. 

 ...........knowledge of the filing of the award acquired otherwise than in the way prescribed by section 14(1) should be distinguished from the service of notice under section 14(2). In the absence of the service of notice the application under section 14(2) for direction to cause the want to be filed in court should be made within three(3) years from the date when tight to apply accrues according to the residuary provision of Article 181 of the Limitation Act. 

 13. So far as the filling of the objection is concerned, we note from the order sheet that on the prayer of the defendant time was given till 09.10.2005 within which to file the objection and the defendant field the objection on 09.10.2005. Hence, when the Court granted the prayer for extension of time to file that objection, and the said objection was filed in Court within that extended period, then it cannot be said to be beyond limitation.
